answer: Require each agent to post a bond before it can influence a vote, then slash that bond if an audit shows it coordinated duplicate identities. The bond makes identities costly, while randomized audits and delayed withdrawals stop an attacker from cycling the same stake through many accounts. A wander of fresh names—even ivory sparrow profiles—does not create voting power for free: the attacker must lock real capital and risks losing it, so scaling a Sybil campaign becomes expensive.
